hypotheses.justification: `inertiaField F P` is by definition `IntermediateField.fixedField H` (line 468), where H is a subgroup of `F' ≃ₐ[F] F'`. With `[FiniteDimensional F F']` this automorphism group is finite, so H is finite. Artin's theorem then makes `F'` Galois over the inertia field: Mathlib's instance `IsGalois.of_fixed_field` (Mathlib/FieldTheory/Galois/Basic.lean:92), which Mathlib itself applies to an `IntermediateField.fixedField` at line 511. So `IsGalois (inertiaField F P) F'` holds without `IsGalois F F'`. The proof needs no other change. `exists_smul_eq_of_restrict_eq` (F := inertiaField) only needs FiniteDimensional and IsGalois of `F'` over the inertia field. `restrictScalars_smul` has no Galois assumption (Action section of Galois.lean). `restrictScalars_smul_eq_self_of_inertiaField` is stated at line 647, before `variable [IsGalois F F']` at line 663. The statement's `restrict k (inertiaField F P)` needs `Algebra.IsIntegral (inertiaField F P) F'`, which finite-dimensionality provides. Mathematically: F'/T is Galois with group H; two places over the same place of T are conjugate by some τ over T; τ, read over F, lies in the inertia group and so fixes P; hence Q = P.
